senses.gloss: (cmp. אֲסִי a. עָשָׂה) to do habitually.—Denom. וֶסֶת, הֶיסֵּת.
[b. h., by way of syncope, forms resembling Kal of סית, as יְסִיתְךָ = יֵיסִי׳, וַיָּסֶת = וַיַּסֶּת &c.] to cause to do, stir up, instigate.
units: <cite ref="Sotah 35a:3">Sot. 35ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>ויהס … אל</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 13:30">Num. XIII, 30</cite>) <he>הִסִּיתָן בדברים</he> (he quieted them, because) he (apparently) instigated them (against Moses).

<cite ref="Chagigah 5a:4">Ḥag. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>עבד שמַסִּיתִין עליו רבו ונִיסַּת וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שרבו מסיתין לו</he>) a slave against whom they incite his master and he (the master) is influenced by the instigation (ed.: a slave whose master, when they incite him, yields &c.), what help is there for him?—

<cite ref="Bava Batra 16a:5">B. Bath. 16ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Job 2:3">Job II, 3</cite>) <he>כביכול כאדם שמסיתין וכ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) like a human being, as it were, that is influenced by instigation.

Ib. יורד ומַסִּית Ms. R. (ed. ומתעה) Satan comes down and incites (to sin). Y. Snh. VII, 25ᵈ top יַסִּית עצמו וכ׳ he will stir himself up (become bold) and incite others; a. fr.—Esp. מַסִּית or מֵסִית (with ref. to Deut. XIII, 7, sq.) he who stirs people up to worship idols.
ib. l. c. מ׳ … בלשון גבוה וכ׳ the massith speaks in a loud voice, the maddiaḥ (v. נָדַח) in a low voice; a. fr.—Pl. מַסִּיתִים, מַסִּיתִין.
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 16:3">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XVI</cite>, end <he>האפיקורסין והמ׳ ומדיחין</he> (ed. Schechter … <he>המינין … המשומדים המסורות</he>).

senses.gloss: to be stirred up, give way to instigation; to be impassioned.
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 89:8">Sifré Deut. 89</cite> <he>מצוה ביד הנ׳ וכ׳</he> he who was to be incited to idolatry must first lay his hand on &c.—Y. Snh. l. c.; Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ bot. <he>מכיון שהוא ניסית וכ׳</he> since he is prevailed upon (to worship idols), he is no longer a wise man.

Yalk. Gen. 127 (play on נ̇פ̇ת̇ל̇י) [read:] נִ֗יסֵּיתִי פּ֗וּתֵּיתֵי ת̇ל̇יתי וכ׳ I was prevailed upon, I was per suaded, I gave my sister the preference over myself; Gen. R. s. 71 (corr. acc.). [For נִיסֵּית she was married, v. נָשָׂא.]
